source.original_text: The determinant of the actual rotated cosine-grid precision is the product of its displayed diagonal values. \det A=\prod_{i=1}^{d}\lambda_i. \(d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge2,\ \kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge2\). Fix every actual \(O\in O(d)\), including either determinant sign. This assertion is pointwise; no Haar-law premise or determinant-one restriction is imposed. For \(i=1,\ldots,d\), define \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i=(\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)\), and the actual precision \(A=O\Lambda O^\top\). Lean uses zero-based \(j.\mathrm{val}+1/2\), corresponding to source \(i=j.\mathrm{val}+1\). The determinant is the genuine real finite determinant and the product ranges over every coordinate once. Orthogonality equations, determinant invariance and the diagonal-product identity are internal proved dependencies. No determinant, spectral-window, positivity or normalization identity is supplied as a new hypothesis. The source bounds are retained exactly, although the determinant algebra itself needs no interval restriction on the diagonal values. The actual Gaussian consumer uses these bounds to obtain positive definiteness from the existing source admissibility result. The real consumer is the same actual \(N(0,A^{-1})\) relative to Euclidean Lebesgue volume. Only its prefactor is independent of \(O\); the quadratic exponent retains the actual hidden orientation. The power \(d/2\) is real, including odd dimensions. The explicit-product density is a mathematical identity. The separate unweighted Gaussian integral/known-normalizer proposition, full C.4 calculus/minimizer, moments/Krylov, operational oracle/precision/TV/cost adapters and both complete main lower bounds remain open.

    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ)
    (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ),
    let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
    let diagonalValue : Fin d → ℝ := fun i =>
      (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)
    let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=

        (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
    A.det = ∏ i : Fin d, diagonalValue i
decoder_context: Fin d is the finite coordinate set with natural values zero through d-1. The notation ∏ i : Fin d, f i is the ordinary finite product containing one factor for every coordinate.

Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) real is the full real orthogonal group. Its carrier requires both products with the transpose to equal identity, and permits either determinant sign. It supplies no probability law, determinant-one filter or algorithmic access.

Matrix.diagonal f is the actual square diagonal matrix with entries f i and zero off the diagonal. Matrix multiplication and transpose are ordinary finite-coordinate operations. The displayed local matrix is constructed from the displayed values and the actual orthogonal element.

Matrix.det is the genuine finite square determinant over real entries, defined by the alternating multilinear/Leibniz determinant. It is not trace, absolute determinant, a determinant sign, an assumed product or a supplied eigenvalue certificate. Equality is equality of real numbers.

Real.pi and Real.cos have their usual real meanings. The casts of the index value and dimension are real; the one-half and grid division are real operations. Division is totalized at zero, while the explicit dimension restriction separately makes its displayed denominator nonzero. All local lets and the conclusion share the same dimension, parameter and orthogonal element.

reconstruction.text:
For every natural number d with d ≥ 2, every real number κ with κ ≥ 2, and every real d by d orthogonal matrix O, make the following definitions. Orthogonality means OOᵀ = OᵀO = I_d; O ranges over the full real orthogonal group, allowing either determinant sign. Index coordinates by the integers i = 0, …, d − 1. For each such i, define θ_i = (i + 1/2)π/d and λ_i = (κ + 1)/2 + ((κ − 1)/2) cos(θ_i). The occurrences of i and d in these formulas are their real casts; 1/2 and every division are real operations. The restriction d ≥ 2 makes the denominator d nonzero.

Let D be the actual d by d diagonal matrix with diagonal entry λ_i in coordinate i and zero off the diagonal, and define the real matrix A = ODOᵀ. Then the genuine real determinant satisfies det(A) = ∏_{i=0}^{d−1} λ_i = ∏_{i=0}^{d−1} [(κ + 1)/2 + ((κ − 1)/2) cos((i + 1/2)π/d)]. Each displayed product is the ordinary full finite product, containing exactly one factor for each of the d coordinates. The angles, the diagonal values, D, and A are defined outputs of the universally chosen inputs d, κ, and O; they are not additional independent inputs or assumed determinant or eigenvalue certificates. All definitions and the equality use the same d, κ, and O.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.DisplacementJacobianEntropy
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Basic
open Matrix
open scoped BigOperators
set_option autoImplicit false
/-!
# Actual fixed-spectrum precision determinant

Zhou--Suzuki, arXiv:2610.20492v1 Eq11 and the determinant component of
Appendix C.4. The actual cosine-grid precision has the displayed diagonal
product as determinant, pointwise for every full real orthogonal O, either
determinant sign. Exactly source d>=2 and kappa>=2 are retained; these bounds
are not needed for this algebraic identity but feed the actual Gaussian
consumer through the existing source admissibility producer.

The existing public DisplacementJacobianEntropy.det_conjStarAlgAut_eq is the
canonical conjugation-invariance proof node and is reused literally here.
No duplicate generic invariant or determinant-one premise is introduced.
The focused Test consumes this exact determinant result, existing actual
admissibility and canonical GaussianPrecisionDensity in the same actual
inverse-precision law, exposing the spectrum-only density coefficient while
retaining the actual hidden orientation in the quadratic exponent.

Unweighted Gaussian-integral/known-Z statements, full C.4 calculus/minimizer,
moments/Krylov, true oracle/TV/precision/cost adapters and main bounds remain
separate. This pointwise identity is fixed-spectrum background, not a
determinant-sign lower-bound claim.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumDeterminant
theorem actual_precision_det {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ)
    (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) :
    let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
    let diagonalValue : Fin d → ℝ := fun i =>
      (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)
    let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) * Matrix.diagonal diagonalValue *
        (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
    A.det = ∏ i : Fin d, diagonalValue i := by
  classical
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let diagonalValue : Fin d → ℝ := fun i =>
    (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)
  let M : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ := O
  change (M * Matrix.diagonal diagonalValue * M.transpose).det =
    ∏ i : Fin d, diagonalValue i
  have hdet :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.DisplacementJacobianEntropy.det_conjStarAlgAut_eq
      (O : unitary (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ)) (Matrix.diagonal diagonalValue)
  rw [Unitary.conjStarAlgAut_apply] at hdet
  change (M * Matrix.diagonal diagonalValue * star M).det =
    (Matrix.diagonal diagonalValue).det at hdet
  have hstar : star M = M.transpose := by
    ext i j
    simp
  rw [hstar, Matrix.det_diagonal] at hdet
  exact hdet
end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumDeterminant
